seoTitle: How to Merge Layers in Canva (Group & Lock Guide)
metaDescription: Group and lock multiple design elements in Canva so they move and scale together, since there's no destructive flatten-merge option.
intro: Canva doesn't have a destructive flatten-merge button like Photoshop, but you can still combine multiple elements so they behave as a single unified layer. This guide covers selecting, grouping, and locking elements together, plus exporting a flattened image when you need one.

steps.heading: Open the Layers panel
steps.body: Locate the Position and Layers panel tab to view your current design elements.

steps.heading: Select multiple elements
steps.body: Use shortcut keys to select several text boxes, graphics, or backgrounds at once on the canvas.

steps.heading: Group the selected objects
steps.body: Use the grouping feature to combine the selected shapes and text layers into a single container.

steps.heading: Adjust scale for grouped layers
steps.body: Resize the group as a whole while keeping the internal proportions intact.

steps.heading: Lock the combined elements
steps.body: Lock the grouped layer to freeze its position and prevent accidental changes.

steps.heading: Export a flattened version
steps.body: When you need a single flattened image, export the grouped section as a high-resolution PNG.

faq.question: Does Canva have a true flatten-merge feature like Photoshop?
faq.answer: No, Canva doesn't offer a destructive merge button, but grouping and locking elements together achieves a similar practical effect.

faq.question: Will grouped elements move together automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, once grouped, elements scale and move as a single unit unless you ungroup them later.

faq.question: How do I get a single flat image from my layers?
faq.answer: Exporting your grouped design as a PNG effectively flattens it into one image file.

faq.question: Can I still edit individual elements after grouping?
faq.answer: Yes, you can ungroup at any time to access and edit the individual elements again.
